title: Asymptotic expansion of the resolvent of the discrete bi-Laplacian at both thresholds for all six resonance types
author: Sisi Huang and Xiaohua Yao
work: Decay estimates for discrete bi-Laplace operators with potentials on the lattice $\Z$
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 1.8 of the article (source label Asymptotic expansion theorem, source0.tex lines 396--443), the complete asymptotic expansion of the resolvent $(M^{\pm}(\mu))^{-1}$ of the discrete bi-Laplace operator with a decaying potential at both thresholds, in the six resonance configurations, delivered with the author's own complete 230-line proof at source0.tex lines 1852--2081. H3: even after the whole delivered apparatus is granted - Definitions 1.4 and 1.5 fixing $Q$, $v_k$, $\widetilde{Q}$, $\widetilde{v}_k$ and the projections $S_j$, $\widetilde{S}_j$, the free-resolvent boundary values $R_0^{\pm}(\mu^4)$ with the weighted-space notation $\B(s,s')$, Lemma 5.1 with its complete proof giving the Puiseux expansions at both thresholds, the resonance-type characterisation of Theorem 1.7 with Remark 5.3, and the Jensen--Nenciu reduction Lemma 5.4 - the solver must still do research-level work for each of the six cases. It must identify the correct leading power of $\mu$ in each resonance case, substitute the right finite Puiseux expansion into $M^{\pm}(\mu)=U+vR^{\pm}_0(\mu^4)v$, run the successive Feshbach reductions on $Q\ell^2$, on $S_0\ell^2$, on $S_1\ell^2$ and on the corresponding tilde spaces, decide invertibility of each leading operator through the kernel identities of Remark 5.3, control all remainder terms $\Gamma$ in the operator norm including the $\mu$-derivative, and reassemble the nested Neumann series into the printed expansions with the exact weights in $\mu^{-1}$, $\mu^{-3}$, $\mu^{-1/2}$ and their companion orders. That chain of threshold analysis, where the decay exponent demanded of the potential (15, 19 or 27 at zero; 7, 11 or 15 at 16) is tied to the resonance type, is far beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
